title: Compare halogen affinities
statement:
Why can electron attachment to Cl release more energy than attachment to F despite F being more electronegative?

[_]{a}

choices: The compact F valence shell increases repulsion for the incoming electron.
Cl gains a proton before attaching an electron.
Electron affinity is defined as removing an electron.
explanations: Attachment trends need more than an electronegativity ranking.

hints: Electron affinity involves a free gaseous atom.
F adds an electron to a compact 2p subshell.
Electron repulsion matters along with attraction.
solution: Electron affinity involves a free gaseous atom. F adds an electron to a compact 2p subshell. Electron repulsion matters along with attraction. Attachment trends need more than an electronegativity ranking.
